title: AAAK Dialect & Closets
lead: A compact symbolic index an LLM can scan in one pass to know which drawer to open.
summary: AAAK is a lossy summarization format that extracts entities, topics, key quotes, emotions, and flags from verbatim drawer content into a single compact line (typically 40-150 bytes). Closets are searchable index collections that hold these pointer lines, each pointing back to the original drawer(s) via the → syntax. During retrieval, the searcher scans closets first to identify which drawers are relevant, then returns verbatim content from those drawers—100% recall is preserved because no information is lost, only indexed. The dialect supports non-Latin scripts (Hindi, Cyrillic, etc.) via language-aware Unicode patterns in the i18n system.

concepts.definition: A structured symbolic summarization format extracting entities (people), topics (key phrases), quotes (5-55 char snippets), emotional tone (3 codes like vul+joy), and importance flags (ORIGIN, CORE, PIVOT) from content into pipe-separated lines readable by any LLM without decompression.

ChromaDB index documents (1500 chars max) holding topic pointers back to drawers. Each line is atomic: topic|entities|→drawer_a,drawer_b. Created during mining, rebuilt on re-mine, queried first during search to identify relevant drawers before fetching verbatim content.

Inspired by Niklas Luhmann's method: small cross-referenced index cards (closets) point to larger verbatim source materials (drawers). The AAAK format makes cards scannable in a single LLM context window, allowing semantic decisions about which drawer to retrieve without loading the drawer itself.

AAAK extracts key signals from content (not a compression) but preserves 100% recall because drawers hold the original verbatim text. Information selected for the index is a subset, but nothing is lost—the retrieval path always returns exact words from the source.

Single-letter abbreviations mapping emotional tone (vul=vulnerability, joy=joy, fear=fear, etc.) extracted from content keywords or metadata. Up to 3 codes per line; helps LLMs prioritize emotionally significant moments during retrieval.

Binary metadata tags (ORIGIN=founding moment, CORE=identity pillar, PIVOT=turning point, SENSITIVE=private) extracted from content keywords or zettel metadata to signal which drawers hold foundational or sensitive information.

Hardcoded set of 50+ common English words that look like proper nouns but are usually sentence-starters (The, When, User) or weekday/month names. Filtered during entity extraction so fake entities don't clutter closet pointers.

Hybrid retrieval optimization: when a searcher matches a closet, it boosts the ranking (up to 0.40) of drawers from that source file. Rank-based (ordinal position) rather than distance-based, more reliable on narrative content where distances cluster.

Localization system supporting combining marks (Devanagari ा ी, Arabic harakat, Thai), Cyrillic, accented Latin. Each language declares boundary_chars to expand Python's \b regex to scripts where word boundaries aren't \w transitions. Closets in any script are extracted identically.

symbols.name: Dialect
symbols.role: Main AAAK encoder. Methods: compress() for plain text, encode_zettel() for structured data, generate_layer1() for essential story, decode() for parsing. Supports entity mapping, language-aware i18n patterns, emotional tone detection, flag extraction.

symbols.name: build_closet_lines
symbols.role: Extracts topics (regex), entities (2+ occurrence proper nouns), quotes from drawer content. Returns list of atomic closet pointer lines ready for upsert. Handles both legacy 3-segment and Tier 6a 4-segment formats.

symbols.name: upsert_closet_lines
symbols.role: Writes closet pointer lines to ChromaDB, packing greedily without splitting lines across closets (1500 char limit). Deterministically numbers closets (_01, _02, …). Always called after purge_file_closets on re-mine.

symbols.name: regenerate_closets
symbols.role: Optional post-mine LLM-assisted closet refinement. Reads drawers, sends content to LLM (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), replaces regex closets with LLM-mined topics/quotes. Locked per source file to avoid races with concurrent mining.

symbols.name: _extract_drawer_ids_from_closet
symbols.role: Parses → notation (→drawer_a,drawer_b) out of closet documents using regex. Preserves order, dedupes. Called during closet-first retrieval to identify which drawers to fetch.

symbols.name: LLMConfig
symbols.role: Holds resolved LLM endpoint/key/model. Validates scheme strictly (http/https only) to prevent exfiltration. Properties: missing() checks what config is needed.

symbols.name: _candidate_entity_words
symbols.role: Finds entity candidate words using i18n-aware patterns from get_entity_patterns(). Handles combining marks via script-aware boundaries. Cached regex objects. Returns all matches from all candidate patterns.

symbols.name: get_entity_patterns
symbols.role: Returns merged entity detection patterns for requested languages. Applies script-aware boundary expansion to handle combining marks. Cached by language tuple. Entry point for i18n in closet extraction.

symbols.name: _script_boundary
symbols.role: Converts Python's \b to script-aware lookaround for non-Latin scripts. Treats declared boundary_chars as inside-word. Essential for Devanagari, Arabic, Hebrew, Thai scripts where combining marks must not be truncated.

symbols.name: CLOSET_CHAR_LIMIT
symbols.role: Hard cap on closet size (1500 chars). Leaves buffer under ChromaDB limits. When adding a line would exceed this, a new closet is created.

symbols.name: CLOSET_EXTRACT_WINDOW
symbols.role: Regex closet extraction scans only first 5000 chars of content (back-of-file is not indexed). Caps CPU cost. LLM closets process up to 30K chars, a key advantage.

symbols.name: CLOSET_RANK_BOOSTS
symbols.role: Ordinal rank-based closet boost values [0.40, 0.25, 0.15, 0.08, 0.04]. Position 0 (best closet match) gets +0.40 distance reduction; position 4 gets +0.04. Applied only if closet distance ≤ 1.5.

surprises.title: Closets Are Secondary Ranking Signal, Not Primary Gate
surprises.detail: The searcher always runs the full drawer query first. Closets boost results, never gate them. Comment (line 826): 'Closets are a ranking SIGNAL, never a first-pass filter... weak-closets regression where narrative content produces low-signal closets... and closet-first routing hides drawers that direct search would find.' This is a deliberate rejection of closet-first indexing in favor of hybrid scoring—100% recall requires never hiding drawers.

surprises.title: Emotion Detection Is Keyword-Based, No LLM
surprises.detail: Plain-text emotion detection (_detect_emotions, line 430) searches for 30+ keywords in lowercase text (love→love, feared→fear, happy→joy). No ML, no API. Result: instant, deterministic, zero tokens. Only 3 codes per line; redundant codes deduped. Fast signal for triage.

surprises.title: Closet_llm Uses Stdlib urllib, Not Requests or SDK
surprises.detail: LLMConfig validates endpoint scheme strictly: if scheme not in ('http', 'https'): raise ValueError. This rejects file:// URLs at parse time, preventing a misconfigured LLM_ENDPOINT from exfiltrating local files. Privacy by architecture, checked on init, not at call time.

surprises.title: Tier 6a Date+Line Locators: Optional but Backward-Compatible
surprises.detail: Closet format supports two variants: legacy 3-segment (topic|entities|→drawer) and Tier 6a 4-segment (topic|entities|YYYY-MM-DD:Lstart-Lend|→drawer). The function emits legacy if metadata is missing or unparseable, so old closets work in new code. New drawers get date+line pointers for jump-to-location on disk.

surprises.title: Regex Closets Have No Stop-Word Filter; Seed Noise
surprises.detail: build_closet_lines() extracts topics via action-verb regex (built|fixed|wrote...) but does NOT filter the matched phrases through a stop-word list. So a topic like 'built the the the' can be extracted verbatim. COCA filter helps with common words (Code, Line), but dialect.py's _STOP_WORDS are not applied to regex closet extraction. This is an inconsistency; dialect closets use _STOP_WORDS, closet_llm ones are manually curated.

designDecisions.decision: Closets as selective index, not filtered cache—always return verbatim from drawers.
designDecisions.rationale: CLAUDE.md principle: 'Verbatim always.' Closets are *pointers* to verbatim content, not summaries. Selection happens at index time (which topics to extract), but nothing is lost from the drawer. Guarantees 100% recall because the original words remain accessible.

designDecisions.decision: Hybrid ranking: drawer query always runs, closets provide boost signal only.
designDecisions.rationale: Prevents weak closets (common in narrative content) from hiding drawers that direct semantic search finds. Line 826: 'weak-closets regression.' Closet distance clustering (1.2-1.5 range) is unreliable on narrative, so ordinal position (rank) is a better signal. Hybrid ensures no perfect-recall regressions.

designDecisions.decision: LLM closet regeneration is optional, regex closets are always available.
designDecisions.rationale: CLAUDE.md principle: 'Local-first, zero external API by default.' Regex closets work offline with zero dependencies, zero tokens. LLM regeneration is an opt-in enhancement for richer indexing (better implicit topic detection, multi-language understanding). Fallback ensures core retrieval never breaks if LLM is unavailable.

designDecisions.decision: Non-Latin scripts supported via script-aware boundaries in i18n patterns, not post-hoc normalization.
designDecisions.rationale: Combining marks (Devanagari, Arabic, Hebrew) are part of the script and must not be stripped. Expanding \b at regex-compile time (via _script_boundary) is simpler and faster than NFD-normalizing text. Patterns are cached per language tuple, amortizing the complexity cost.

designDecisions.decision: Emotion codes are hardcoded keyword-based, not learned embeddings.
designDecisions.rationale: Performance & privacy. Keyword matching is O(1), LLM calls would add latency + tokens. Codes are universal (30+ emotions mapped to 2-4 char codes), deterministic, and transparent. Sufficient signal for triage without ML.

stats.label: Importance flags
stats.value: 6 types (ORIGIN, CORE, PIVOT, SENSITIVE, GENESIS, DECISION, TECHNICAL)

related.why: AAAK closets are the index layer of the palace model; drawers hold the verbatim content closets point to.
Project mining calls build_closet_lines() during file ingest to create closets alongside drawers.
Retrieval uses closet-first hybrid ranking: closets scan fast, then boost matching drawers in the final score.
Entity extraction in closets uses i18n-aware patterns from entity_detector and i18n to handle non-Latin scripts.
Closet entity detection relies on i18n patterns and script-aware boundaries to support Devanagari, Cyrillic, Arabic, etc.
Optional LLM-assisted closet refinement (closet_llm.py) uses configured external endpoints to enhance regex closets.

searchDoc.title: AAAK Dialect & Closets
searchDoc.summary: AAAK is a lossy symbolic summarization format that turns verbatim drawer content into compact closet pointer lines an LLM can scan in one pass. Closets index drawers; retrieval scans closets to boost matching drawers while always returning verbatim content, preserving 100% recall.
searchDoc.body: AAAK Dialect and Closets are the index layer of the MemPalace ingestion pipeline. Drawers hold verbatim 800-character chunks of content; closets are a thin searchable index on top of them, modeled on the Zettelkasten method where small cross-referenced index cards point to larger source materials. AAAK is the dialect that turns a drawer into a closet line: a single compact pipe-separated line (typically 40 to 150 bytes) holding extracted entities, topics, key quotes, emotion codes, and importance flags. AAAK is explicitly NOT lossless compression; the original text cannot be reconstructed from AAAK output. Instead it is a structured summary layer that points back to the original verbatim drawers via the arrow syntax, so 100 percent recall is preserved because nothing is lost, only indexed. During mining, build_closet_lines in palace.py extracts topics via an action-verb regex (built, fixed, wrote, added, pushed, deployed), entities as proper nouns appearing two or more times in a 5000-character extraction window, and quotes as double-quoted strings, filtering entities against a hardcoded stoplist and the COCA corpus. Lines are packed greedily into closets capped at 1500 characters, never splitting a line across closets, rolling to numbered closets when full. Dialect.compress turns any plain text into AAAK by detecting emotional tone and importance flags through keyword matching, ranking topics with TF-IDF plus a proper-noun boost, and scoring a key sentence. Emotion detection uses 30 plus hardcoded keyword mappings with no machine learning and no API calls, making it instant, deterministic, and zero-token. During search the searcher queries closets and drawers in parallel; closets are a ranking signal, never a gate. A drawer from a source whose closet matched receives an ordinal rank-based boost from CLOSET_RANK_BOOSTS of 0.40, 0.25, 0.15, 0.08, 0.04, applied only when closet distance is at most 1.5, because closet distances cluster in the 1.2 to 1.5 range on narrative content and ordinal position is the more reliable signal. Non-Latin scripts are supported through i18n script-aware boundaries: _script_boundary replaces Python's word boundary with a lookaround so Devanagari, Arabic, Hebrew, and Thai combining marks are treated as inside-word, preventing names from being truncated. LLM-assisted closet regeneration via closet_llm is completely optional; regex closets always work offline, and LLMConfig rejects non-HTTP endpoint schemes at init to prevent exfiltration. Layer 1 generation pulls high-weight and flagged moments into a wake-up summary an LLM can scan in one shot.
